title: Prefer generics when the variation is type-level rather than source-shape repetition
task: Review a declarative macro that duplicates one algorithm for several input types even though the behavior is otherwise identical.
context: Each expansion differs only in the concrete type.
A trait bound can express the required operations.
The macro makes diagnostics point into generated expansion rather than the generic algorithm.
evidence: No source-syntax generation or identifier construction is required.
The generic implementation compiles for all current types.
Runtime behavior is identical across expansions.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep the macro because it removes repeated source code.
Prefer metaprogramming because it is more idiomatic Rust.
Add a procedural macro for even more flexibility.
expected_decision_properties: Prefer a generic/trait-bound implementation when it expresses the contract directly.
Reserve macros for source transformations that ordinary functions/generics cannot express ergonomically.
Include compile-time and diagnostic quality in the decision.
unacceptable_reasoning: Macros are always better than duplicated generic code.
Any repeated syntax justifies code generation.
Fewer handwritten lines automatically means lower complexity.
verification_expectations: Compile all current call sites after replacing the macro.
Check compiler diagnostics for representative invalid inputs.
notes: Grounded in Rust for Rustaceans Chapter 7 guidance on declarative/procedural macros and generic alternatives.
